s: Centralized repository for ML features providing consistent training/serving values with low-latency online access.
w: Features (user age, purchase count, item category, session duration) are computed in batch pipelines and stored with point-in-time correctness for training. Online serving stores the latest feature values in a fast KV store (Redis/DynamoDB) for real-time inference. The feature store guarantees training/serving consistency - no training/serving skew. Feature versioning, monitoring, and backfill capabilities are built in.
use: ML model serving requiring pre-computed features at low latency (<10ms)
Preventing training/serving skew where feature computation differs between training and inference
Feature sharing across multiple ML models (recommendation + fraud + ranking use same user features)
Regulatory compliance requiring feature lineage and reproducibility
avoid: Simple ML with few hand-crafted features (pandas + Redis is sufficient)
Deep learning models where features are learned end-to-end from raw data
Small teams without ML platform engineering capacity

props.online_store: Redis | DynamoDB for low-latency feature serving

pat.d: Training features snapshot at event time to prevent future leakage.

pits: Training/serving skew silently degrading model performance - feature store eliminates this but requires adoption discipline
Feature freshness lag impacting model quality - monitor feature staleness per feature
tips: Training/serving skew is THE problem feature stores solve - explain it clearly
Feature store vs data warehouse: feature store is low-latency serving for ML, warehouse is for analytics
